text:
Like the scales of a great sea serpent, sunlight glimmers off the mantles of a spiera shoal that race beneath the waves. With the use 
of forward facing siphuncles and numerous expelling jets, spiera squid are an agile and overpowering shoal. Launching into schools 
of fi sh, grasping morsels of flesh in their fanged tentacles and continuing onward before the scent of blood attracts larger predators. 
When chancing upon enormous creatures like cetaceans and gigantic basking sharks, the shoal charges forward in a blinding stream of 
bubbles. With a sickening sequence of deeply heard thuds, dozens of squid slam their chitin-hardened mantle spears into the flesh of 
their prey, their long tentacles holding on tight as they feast on the quickly sinking creature before it falls too far into the black depths.

Water Breathing Th e spiera can breathe only underwater.
Under Current Th e spiera has Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) 
checks made while underwater.
Shoal Swarm When the spiera makes an attack, any other friendly 
spiera within 5 ft. of it can use its Reaction to make an attack 
against the same target. Th e spiera executing Reaction attacks do 
not generate further Reaction attacks by other spiera in proximity 
to them.

Encountering In the open waters surrounding the coasts of 
Sol’Kesh, spiera shoals are often found dashing under the waves 
at incredible speeds. Chasing a shoal down is nearly impossible 
as they will weave and rush around any pursuers. Often, the 
most effective way of catching the squid is to bait them with a 
large floating carcass, catching them in the act of taking morsels 
of flesh in their hooked beaks. 
Multiattack Th e spiera makes two attacks, using Spearing 
Mantle, Hooked Tentacles and Scissor Beak in any combination.
Spearing Mantle Melee Attack Roll: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one 
target. Hit: 6 (1d8 + 2) Piercing damage. If the spiera swam 20+ 
ft. straight toward the target creature immediately before the 
hit, the target takes an extra 9 (2d8) Piercing damage.
Hooked Tentacles Melee Attack Roll: +4 to hit, reach 10 ft., one 
target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) Slashing damage. If the target is a Normal 
or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (Escape DC 
14). Until this Grapple ends, the target is Restrained, and the 
spiera cannot use its tentacles on another target.
Scissor Beak Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one 
target. Hit: 7 (2d4 + 2) Piercing damage. If the targeted creature 
is Restrained by the spiera’s Hooked Tentacle attack, the spiera 
has Advantage on its Scissor Beak attack.
Ink Cloud (1/Day) Trigger: While it is underwater, and a creature 
the spiera can see hits it with an attack roll Response - A 20 ft. 
radius cloud of ink spreads from the spiera. Th e area is heavily 
obscured for 1 minute, although a signifi cant current can disperse 
the ink. After releasing the ink, the spiera can use the Dash action.
Speed 0 ft., swim 60 ft.
Wary Instinct (1/Day) When startled, the shoal spreads a billowing 
black cloud in unison, obscuring great swaths of the ocean.
Reaction - Trigger: When a friendly spiera that it can see within 30 
ft. of it releases its Ink Cloud. Response - Wisdom Saving Th row: DC 
10, the spiera. Success: The spiera uses its Ink Cloud unless it had 
already used it that day.
Nearly a dozen jets encircle the mantle’s collar. 
With precise control, the squid can contract each 
funnel muscle to direct the water coursing through 
its siphuncle to change directly effortlessly and 
speed through the water in quick measured bursts
A bladed edge to the mantle allows 
the squid to slice through the water 
in blisteringly fast speeds, as well as 
plunge deeply into the flesh of prey
While most cephalopod’s beaks rest 
deep within the mouth, the spiera’s 
extends outward to quickly pierce 
and grip meat as it competes even 
with its own shoal for food
The two long tentacles drag behind the squid, hiding wickedly sharp 
hooks within gripping suction cups. As the spiera swims along large 
prey, these tentacles whip out and latch onto the flesh, anchoring 
the creature to dig its beak in and feast
